privacy.intro: Voice input doesn't need a round trip to the cloud. Start local, and decide what else you want to connect.
privacy.link: Read the details, not just the promise →
privacy.local.title: Local speech stays local.
privacy.local.body: With local Qwen recognition, audio is processed on your Mac, not uploaded. Download the speech model separately, then dictate offline.
privacy.cloud.title: Cloud is a choice, not a catch.
privacy.cloud.body: Optional cloud recognition sends audio to the speech provider you configure. Optional AI sends the text needed for polishing, editing, or translation to your own AI provider.
privacy.history.title: Your history lives with you.
privacy.history.body: Dictation history and diagnostic logs stay on your Mac. Logs are bounded to 15 MB and exclude audio, transcripts, API keys, and prompts. Nothing is automatically uploaded.
privacy.open.title: An app you can look inside.
privacy.open.body: Talkless is source available and distributed directly on GitHub. The app does not collect telemetry. This website has no analytics or tracking scripts; its host may keep standard request logs.
faq.title: A few good questions.
faq.mac.q: Will it work on my Mac?
faq.mac.a: Talkless requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26 or later. Intel Macs and older macOS versions aren't supported. The current release is a beta, so expect a few rough edges.
faq.setup.q: What does getting started look like?
faq.setup.a: Download the DMG, drag Talkless into Applications, and open it. The setup guide walks you through Microphone and Accessibility permissions. Then download the local speech model in Settings → Speech recognition. AI setup is entirely optional.
faq.offline.q: Do I need an account or a subscription?
faq.offline.a: No Talkless account is required. Local recognition runs on your Mac after the model download, with no hosted Talkless service. If you choose cloud speech or AI features, bring your own provider credentials and check that provider's pricing and privacy policy.
faq.apps.q: Does it replace my keyboard or input method?
faq.apps.a: Neither. Talkless lives in the menu bar and inserts text into the field you're using. Keep that field focused until the result arrives. Some apps restrict text insertion or access to selected text; the user guide explains the controls and limitations.
faq.language.q: Can I use it in English and Chinese?
faq.language.a: The app interface supports English and Simplified Chinese. Recognition language support depends on your selected speech engine and model. Optional AI translation and output language settings are separate from the interface language.
faq.help.q: Where do I find help or report a bug?
faq.help.a: Start with the user guide for setup and shortcuts. Our support page covers common problems and what to include when reporting a bug.

guide.meta.title: User guide — Talkless
guide.meta.description: Install Talkless, set up local speech recognition, and learn the dictation, polishing and translation controls.
guide.eyebrow: A SMALL GUIDE TO GETTING STARTED
guide.title:
From a thought
to a text field.
guide.intro: Start with local dictation. Add cloud speech or AI only if you want them. No Talkless account is needed.
guide.install.title: Install and prepare
guide.install.first: Use an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26 or later. Download the beta, open the DMG, and drag Talkless into Applications. Open that copy of the app.
guide.install.permissions: Follow the setup guide to allow Microphone and Accessibility access. Microphone records your voice; Accessibility enables shortcuts and text insertion. Skipping setup does not grant these permissions.
guide.install.model: In Settings → Speech recognition, download the local Qwen3 ASR · 0.6B model (about 713 MB). Wait for verification and preparation to finish. Model weights are separate from the app and are not hosted by Talkless.
guide.shortcuts.title: Speak and finish
guide.shortcuts.body: Click a text field, hold Fn, speak, and release. Tap-to-toggle mode is also available in Settings → Dictation. Pausing your speech does not end a recording. Escape cancels recording or processing.
guide.shortcuts.focus: Keep the intended text field focused until the result arrives. Talkless pastes at the current cursor using the clipboard, then restores the previous clipboard unless you copied something else. Recover finished text from History if needed.
guide.shortcuts.keys: Fn is the default, not a requirement. Set the dictation key and AI polishing shortcut in Dictation settings. If Fn opens the emoji panel, change the Globe-key action to Do Nothing in macOS Keyboard settings, or use another key.
guide.speech.title: Choose your speech engine
guide.speech.body: Local Qwen and Apple on-device recognition can work offline after their required models are available. They provide live text. Cloud Whisper-compatible recognition sends the full recording to your configured provider after you finish, and may incur charges.
guide.speech.mic: Choose System default or a specific microphone in Settings → Dictation. A disconnected selected microphone is not silently replaced. If the input route changes during a recording, check the device and start again.
guide.ai.title: Use AI only when you want it
guide.ai.body: Configure your own provider, credentials and model in Settings → AI service. Polishing is off by default. During recording, the AI polishing shortcut (Right Option by default) finishes this input and does the opposite of your saved polishing default: Use AI polishing or Skip AI polishing. It does not change that default.
guide.ai.more: Voice editing is separately enabled in Dictation settings: select text and speak an editing instruction. Translation uses Control-Option-T by default: select text, review the result, then Copy or Replace Original. These features send the needed text to your AI provider. Review output before relying on it.
guide.dictionary.title: Keep useful words and results
guide.dictionary.body: Add preferred spellings in Settings → Dictionary. Blue dictionary marks mean a confirmed spelling is present, not that a correction is guaranteed. Review suggestions come from local comparisons of raw and polished history; only terms you accept join your dictionary.
guide.dictionary.history: History keeps up to 500 recent results on your Mac. Copy or delete entries there. Clearing history and clearing daily activity are separate actions. Interface language, recognition language and AI output language are separate settings too.
privacy.meta.title: Privacy — Talkless
privacy.meta.description: What stays on your Mac, what optional providers receive, and how Talkless stores credentials, history and diagnostics.
privacy.page.title:
Local by default.
Specific about the rest.
privacy.page.intro: Local-first is a starting point, not a blanket promise that every feature is offline. Here is how the app and this website handle data.
privacy.audio.title: Speech and model downloads
privacy.audio.body: Local Qwen processes audio on your Mac. Apple recognition runs on-device after required assets are available. Downloading models contacts the model source you choose; Talkless does not host the weights. Optional cloud recognition uploads the full recording and dictionary hints to your speech provider.
privacy.requests.title: Optional AI requests
privacy.requests.body: Polishing sends the transcript, dictionary hints and editing instructions. App-aware tone can include the foreground app and its writing context. Your additional instructions and output language are included when set. Voice editing sends the selection and spoken instruction; translation sends the selection and language instructions.
privacy.requests.choice: Opening AI settings does not send your text. Fetch Models and Test Connection are explicit network actions; a connection test uses a fixed sample, not your dictation. Provider pricing, processing and retention policies apply. Talkless cannot guarantee a provider’s privacy practices.
privacy.storage.title: History and credentials
privacy.storage.body: Preferences and dictionary terms use macOS UserDefaults. AI service keys use macOS Keychain. Important: the separate cloud speech-recognition key is currently stored in plaintext in UserDefaults, not Keychain.
privacy.storage.history: Models, text history, text-free daily totals and diagnostics live in your Mac’s Library/Application Support/Talkless folder. History contains text, not audio, and holds up to 500 results. Delete saved text in History; clear daily activity separately. Daily totals are retained for 400 calendar days.
privacy.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics you choose to share
privacy.diagnostics.body: Event logs are bounded to 15 MB and exclude audio, transcripts, API keys and prompts. Export diagnostics creates a local ZIP; it does not upload it. Optional macOS crash reports can contain personal information and file paths. Inspect an export before sharing it.
privacy.website.title: This website and distribution
privacy.website.body: The app does not collect telemetry. This website has no analytics, tracking scripts, remote fonts or microphone access. Its host may keep standard request logs. The demo uses sample text in your browser. The language preference is stored locally when available.
privacy.website.download: Download buttons use this site’s /download address, then redirect to the published GitHub release asset. GitHub handles that download under its own policies. Talkless is source available: you can inspect the repository from the single GitHub link in the header. This wording does not grant a software license.

updates.current.title: Current beta
updates.changed.title: What changed
updates.install.title: Install or update
updates.install.body: The download is a Developer ID signed and notarized disk image for Apple Silicon and macOS 26+. Open it and drag Talkless into Applications. If you already use Talkless, Check for Updates is available from its menu bar menu. You choose when to download and install.
updates.beta.title: A note about betas
updates.beta.body: Beta builds can have rough edges. Update checks follow your selected Stable or Beta channel. Switching back to Stable does not downgrade an installed beta. Speech models are downloaded separately and are not bundled with app updates.
support.meta.title: Support — Talkless
support.meta.description: Troubleshoot permissions, speech models, text insertion and AI connections, and prepare a useful Talkless bug report.
support.eyebrow: WHEN SOMETHING GETS IN THE WAY
support.title:
Let’s get your
words moving again.
support.intro: Try the checks below first. They cover the most common reasons a dictation does not start or reach your text field.
support.recording.title: Recording will not start
support.recording.body: Check Microphone and Accessibility in macOS Privacy & Security, then reopen Talkless if macOS asks. In Dictation settings, verify the selected microphone is connected. Try System default or another available input. If a device disconnects or its route changes, start a new recording.
support.model.title: The model is not ready
support.model.body: Open Settings → Speech recognition. Let the download finish verifying and preparing, or retry a failed download. If your network cannot reach the selected source, choose another supported mirror. For Apple recognition, check the selected language and its speech assets.
support.text.title: Text went missing or landed elsewhere
support.text.body: Keep the intended text field focused until processing finishes. Check History for the completed result and copy it again. Some apps restrict pasting or exposing selected text. Try a normal text field in Notes to narrow down whether the issue belongs to one app.
support.ai.title: AI is unavailable
support.ai.body: Check your provider, key and model in AI service settings. Configuration complete is not proof of a successful connection. Test Connection sends a fixed sample and may incur a provider charge. A polishing failure keeps the original transcript; translation and voice editing show their own errors. Never share your API key in a bug report.
support.report.title: Report a reproducible problem
support.report.body: Use the GitHub repository link in the header, then choose Issues. Include your Talkless version and build, macOS version, Mac model, speech engine, microphone and clear steps to reproduce. Say what you expected and what actually happened. This website does not collect or submit reports.
support.report.diagnostics: If diagnostics would help, use Settings → System → Diagnostics to export a local ZIP. Review its contents before attaching it; optional crash reports may include personal information and file paths. Nothing is automatically uploaded. Avoid sharing private dictation or selected text.
release.note.0: Dictionary review merges suggestions without regard to case, skips capitalization-only changes, and avoids recommending existing terms again while preserving saved spellings.
release.note.1: Removed the explanatory language-change hint from the translation panel.
release.note.2: Translation shortcut capture now asks for a key combination, while dictation capture still asks for a single key.
release.note.3: The completion checkmark now stays for 50 milliseconds after insertion instead of two seconds.
